Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) show that there will be approximately 232,600 teaching coordinators on the job in 2024, and the number is expected to rise to 235,500 by 2034, with a net increase of approximately 2,900 positions, an average of approximately 21,900 vacancies per year, and a median annual salary of approximately US$74,700 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace instructional coordinators, but it will reshape the workflow of Instructional Coordinators: handing over repetitive and structurable tasks to tools, people will focus on judgment, responsibility and creativity. subject.summary: Instructional Coordinators are a profession that puts professional judgment and responsibility on their shoulders: AI accelerates structured tasks, but the core decision-making is still completed by humans. Let’s explain clearly “what to do, what to be afraid of, and whether it’s worth it”.
